name: pairwise alignment by dynamic programming
mechanism: fill a table over prefix pairs of two sequences where each cell holds the best cost of aligning those prefixes from its three neighbours (match or substitute, insert, delete), then read the corner or trace back the path

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Levenshtein edit distance' in section Combinatorial algorithms / Sequence algorithms / Approximate sequence matching: computes a metric for the amount of difference between two sequences
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Damerau–Levenshtein distance': computes a distance measure between two strings, improves on Levenshtein distance
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Needleman–Wunsch algorithm': find global alignment between two sequences
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Smith–Waterman algorithm': find local sequence alignment
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Hirschberg's algorithm': finds the least cost sequence alignment between two sequences, as measured by their Levenshtein distance
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Dynamic time warping': measure similarity between two sequences which may vary in time or speed
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Longest common subsequence problem': Find the longest subsequence common to all sequences in a set of sequences
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Shortest common supersequence problem': Find the shortest supersequence that contains two or more sequences as subsequences
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Longest common substring problem': find the longest string (or strings) that is a substring (or are substrings) of two or more strings

requires: a cost for substitution, insertion, deletion (policy)
two sequences over a common alphabet
fails_when: quadratic space and time in sequence length
the cost table is a human prior; changing it changes every distance
